question:
A 63-year-old man presents to the clinic for an evaluation of intense itching of his right thigh region for
the past few days. He states some ‘red bumps’ just began to form. The patient mentions that he was
recently at a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes
mellitus type 2, and hyperlipidemia. He takes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He does not
smoke or drink. His vitals are within normal limits today. On physical examination, a linear line with 3
red papules is present along the medial aspect of his right thigh. Additionally, there are small rows of
bumps on his left leg and right forearm. Excoriations are also apparent in the same region. Which of
the following is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Folliculitis (B) Poison ivy dermatitis (C)
Allergic reaction to clothing material (D) Scabies (E) Flea bites (F) Cutaneous larva migrans (G)
Contact dermatitis (H) Dermatophytosis (I) Chigger bites (J) Bedbug bite
 A. Allergic reaction to clothing material
B. Dermatophytosis
C. Contact dermatitis
D. Flea bites
E. Poison ivy dermatitis
F. Folliculitis
G. Chigger bites

H. Bedbug bite
I. Scabies
J. Cutaneous larva migrans
